Single: Runs every frame for the parameters chosen below. \n\n Sweep: Compares one frame across different subset and strain-window sizes at a chosen subset overlap.
Step size given as subset ÷ N(Larger N means denser correlation). Capped between 2 and 6.
How much neighbouring subsets cover each other. Typical values are 0.50–0.75.
Total No. of analyses = No. of subsets × No. of strain windows.
Min to Max (px) capped by the image/ROI(Odd subset sizes) and speckle pattern.

Min to Max, in data points (odd values). Each subset\'s step turns a window into a VSG of (window − 1) × step + 1 px, which is the sweep\'s y axis. Larger windows smooth strain more; smaller ones resolve finer gradients.
Strains along the axis through the ROI centre are monitored.
No combination fits this ceiling — raise Max strain window or lower the subset range.
